blockMcqs.question: What core decision must a multi-elevator system make?
options: Which floor to build next
Which car answers which request
How many buttons to install
What color to paint the cabin
blockMcqs.explanation: The snapshot frames the problem as deciding which of several cars should serve each request while minimizing wait time.

blockMcqs.question: Which of these is a functional requirement here?
options: The system must be fair to all requests
The system must accept internal cabin requests
The system must scale to any building
The system must never lose state
blockMcqs.explanation: Accepting internal (cabin) button requests is a functional requirement; fairness and scaling are non-functional concerns covered separately.

blockMcqs.question: In noun extraction, what does "pick the best elevator" become?
options: A field on the Elevator class
A dispatch strategy owned by the controller
A new enum value
Part of the Floor class
blockMcqs.explanation: Verbs describing decisions become behaviors pulled into a strategy owned by the controller, not fields on a data class like Elevator.

blockMcqs.question: Why does Request separate sourceFloor from destinationFloor?
options: For no real reason, just style
Because external requests only know a source floor and direction until boarded
Because destinationFloor is always required
To reduce the size of the Elevator class
blockMcqs.explanation: An external hallway call only has a source floor and direction — the destination isn't known until the rider boards and presses a cabin button.

blockMcqs.question: What does Elevator.addStop() do when direction is IDLE?
options: Rejects the stop
Sets direction based on whether the floor is above or below
Always sets direction to UP
Waits for another elevator
blockMcqs.explanation: When idle, adding a stop sets direction toward that floor (UP if above current floor, DOWN if below) so the car starts moving correctly.

blockMcqs.question: What role does ElevatorController play in the design?
options: It replaces the Elevator class entirely
It's the single coordinator that delegates assignment to a strategy
It only renders the display panel
It stores historical ride data
blockMcqs.explanation: ElevatorController owns all elevators and delegates the 'which car' decision to a pluggable DispatchStrategy rather than deciding itself.

blockMcqs.question: In SCAN, what does canServe() prevent?
options: A car from ever stopping
A car mid-sweep from doubling back for an opposite-direction request
Two cars from existing on the same floor
The controller from accepting new requests
blockMcqs.explanation: canServe() only lets a car take requests consistent with its current sweep direction, so it never reverses mid-sweep to grab one call.

blockMcqs.question: Which pattern powers pushing floor updates to displays?
options: Strategy
State
Observer
Factory
blockMcqs.explanation: The pattern table maps Observer to Elevator.notifyDisplays(), which pushes updates to listeners without the elevator knowing who they are.

blockMcqs.question: Why is nearest-idle-car dispatch considered naive?
options: It's too slow to compute
It ignores cars already moving toward the requested floor
It never picks a valid elevator
It requires no locking at all
blockMcqs.explanation: Nearest-idle-car only looks at idle cars, missing a moving car that would pass the requested floor for nearly free.

blockMcqs.question: How does LOOK improve on plain SCAN?
options: It ignores hallway requests
It reverses early once no requests remain ahead, skipping empty floors
It always uses the nearest car
It removes the need for a dispatcher
blockMcqs.explanation: LOOK behaves like SCAN but reverses as soon as no pending requests remain ahead, avoiding a sweep to the building's end with no purpose.

blockMcqs.question: What causes the duplicate-assignment concurrency bug?
options: A missing Direction enum value
Read-then-decide over shared elevator state without synchronization
Using Strategy instead of Factory
Storing requests in a SortedSet
blockMcqs.explanation: Two requests reading the same elevator as 'closest' before either assignment is committed is a classic race over shared mutable state.

blockMcqs.question: Why do internal requests bypass ElevatorController?
options: Internal requests are less important
The rider already boarded a specific car, so no assignment is needed
The controller cannot access InternalPanel
Internal requests use a different lock
blockMcqs.explanation: Since the rider already chose a car by boarding it, addStop() can be called directly — there's no 'which elevator' decision left to make.

blockMcqs.question: Why use one central controller instead of self-assigning cars?
options: It's required by building safety codes
It avoids needing distributed consensus among cars sharing one building
It makes each elevator faster
It removes the need for a dispatch strategy
blockMcqs.explanation: A single coordinator avoids the complexity of cars needing full visibility into each other's state just to avoid duplicate assignments.
